forces.title: Automotive retail pivoting to AI-driven, data-centric customer experiences
forces.description: The automotive industry is undergoing a fundamental shift from product-centric to data-centric mobility, where customer intelligence, predictive engagement, and continuous relationships are becoming paramount. This transformation extends to two- and three-wheelers, with AI expected to define the next competitive battle in retail by enabling personalized advisory experiences, improved lead management, and proactive aftersales support. This structural shift necessitates significant technology investments and operational restructuring.
forces.source_title: AI will define the next battle in automotive retail

forces.title: Rapid EV adoption in high-utilization 2W/3W segments
forces.description: India's EV adoption is accelerating significantly in high-utilization segments such as two-wheelers and three-wheelers, including fleet operations. This momentum creates strong demand for AI-driven solutions like predictive maintenance, battery-health forecasting, and intelligent charging management. These technologies are critical for improving asset productivity, operational efficiency, and profitability, directly benefiting manufacturers and operators in the 2W/3W EV space.
forces.source_title: AI will define the next battle in automotive retail

forces.title: Government policies and incentives driving EV adoption
forces.description: Multiple government schemes and policies, including PM E-DRIVE (FAME III), FAME India Phase-II, and the Electric Mobility Promotion Scheme (EMPS 2024), provide substantial financial incentives and subsidies for the purchase of electric two-wheelers (e-2W) and electric three-wheelers (e-3W). These initiatives significantly reduce the upfront cost for consumers and operators, directly boosting sales and market penetration of EVs in the 2W/3W segment.

forces.title: Reduced GST and customs duties fostering EV ecosystem
forces.description: The government has lowered GST on electric vehicles from 12% to 5% and on EV chargers/charging stations from 18% to 5%. Additionally, a 100% customs duty exemption was granted on 25 critical minerals essential for EV battery production. These fiscal measures significantly reduce costs across the EV value chain, making electric two- and three-wheelers more affordable and accelerating the development of the domestic EV manufacturing ecosystem.

forces.title: Expanding EV charging infrastructure supporting wider adoption
forces.description: India's EV charging network is expanding rapidly, with public charging stations reaching 29,151 by Q3 FY25. The government plans to add approximately 72,000 new EV chargers by FY26, backed by schemes like FAME India Phase-II which approved capital subsidies for 7,432 EV public charging stations. This extensive development of charging infrastructure addresses a key barrier to EV adoption, facilitating convenience for 2W/3W EV users.

forces.title: Increasing OEM investments in EV and battery manufacturing
forces.description: Major players in the two- and three-wheeler segments are making significant investments in EV technology and battery manufacturing. Ola Electric is developing proprietary cell manufacturing (Bharat Cell) with a target of 5 GWh capacity by FY26, while TVS Motor and Hero MotoCorp plan substantial capital expenditures to expand capacity, product development, and scale EV operations. These investments aim to strengthen localization, manage costs, and drive innovation in the EV value chain.

forces.title: Strategic partnerships driving electric three-wheeler development
forces.description: Collaborations like the Joint Development Agreement between Hyundai Motor and TVS Motor to develop and commercialize electric three-wheelers for last-mile mobility signify a concerted effort to innovate in this segment. Such partnerships accelerate product development, enhance technological capabilities, and facilitate market penetration for electric 3-wheelers in India and other markets, catering to growing demand for sustainable and efficient urban transport solutions.

forces.title: Customized financing solutions boosting EV accessibility
forces.description: Partnerships between EV manufacturers and financial institutions, such as Euler Motors with Annapurna Finance, are expanding customized financing options for electric three-wheelers. These initiatives offer improved EV access for fleet operators, small businesses, and last-mile delivery entrepreneurs by providing flexible repayment options and competitive interest rates. Enhanced financing availability reduces the financial barrier to EV adoption, stimulating demand across various commercial applications.

forces.title: Strong export demand supporting overall auto sector growth
forces.description: Automobile exports from India increased by 24% YoY in FY26, reaching over 6.7 million units, driven by robust international demand for passenger vehicles, two-wheelers, and commercial vehicles. This strong export performance indicates global competitiveness and diversified revenue streams for Indian manufacturers, including those in the 2W/3W segment, contributing to overall industry growth and stability despite potential domestic market fluctuations.

forces.title: NITI Aayog proposes shift to mandates over subsidies for EV policy
forces.description: NITI Aayog has proposed a national EV policy that emphasizes mandates and disincentives rather than solely relying on subsidies, aiming for 30% EV share of total vehicle sales by 2030. This potential shift signals a more forceful approach to accelerate EV adoption, including for 2W/3W. While potentially reducing direct financial support, it could introduce regulatory drivers that create more sustained and predictable demand for electric vehicles.

forces.title: Consumer hesitation and misinformation on EV adoption
forces.description: A significant proportion of consumer hesitation surrounding EV adoption stems from uncertainty rather than product limitations. Prospective buyers frequently have questions about charging access, range performance, battery degradation, resale prospects, and emergency support. Addressing these concerns requires ongoing, personalized engagement and education, posing a challenge to mass-market EV penetration, particularly in cost-sensitive segments like two- and three-wheelers.

viewpoints.title: AI to drive automotive retail differentiation, crucial for mass EV adoption
viewpoints.description: KPMG believes AI will be as important as electrification in the next phase of automotive competition, shifting differentiation from products to customer experiences. For India, AI can address profitability challenges in dealerships by improving lead qualification, personalized communication, and aftersales. This is particularly relevant for 2W/3W EVs, which are gaining rapid momentum in high-utilization segments, where AI-driven predictive maintenance and charging management will enhance asset productivity and profitability.
viewpoints.source_title: AI will define the next battle in automotive retail

viewpoints.title: India’s EV market poised for strong growth, led by 2W and 3W segments
viewpoints.description: The Indian electric vehicle (EV) market is set for robust and sustained growth through 2030, largely due to increasing company focus and strong government support. Two-wheelers and three-wheelers are identified as the dominant categories, making up approximately 87% of total EV sales in FY26. This indicates a significant structural shift and strong growth prospects for the two- and three-wheeler segments.

viewpoints.title: India is the world's leading manufacturer of electric 2W and 3W vehicles
viewpoints.description: India has emerged as the largest manufacturer globally for electric two-wheelers (E2W) and electric three-wheelers (E3W). This leadership position underscores India's significant capabilities and scale in these critical EV segments, contributing to its overall automotive industry growth and positioning it as a key player in the global electric mobility landscape, especially in the last-mile and personal mobility sectors.

viewpoints.title: State policies and increasing income levels driving 2W EV sales in key states
viewpoints.description: Maharashtra is leading in 2W EV sales for FY26, primarily driven by rising income levels among consumers and supportive government regulations. This trend highlights the localized impact of economic prosperity and targeted policies in accelerating EV adoption within the two-wheeler segment, demonstrating how regional factors contribute significantly to overall market growth and penetration across India.

demand_drivers.description: Supportive government policies and schemes like PM E-DRIVE (FAME III) and EMPS 2024 are accelerating EV adoption and manufacturing.
Automotive companies are shifting their strategies and investments towards the EV segment, launching new models and expanding production.

market_sizing.methodology: Total EV sales in India for FY26. Two-wheelers and three-wheelers constituted approximately 87% of this volume, making them the dominant segments within the overall EV market.

demand_drivers.description: Government-mandated objectives to increase EV penetration significantly across segments, especially 2W and 3W.
A shared governmental and industry goal to mitigate environmental impact by promoting electric mobility.

new_opportunities.description: The ambitious target of 80% EV penetration in 2W/3W by 2030 represents a huge market opportunity for manufacturers, infrastructure providers, and component suppliers.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Massive EV adoption in 2W and 3W segments

market_sizing.methodology: Government objective for EV sales penetration target across vehicle categories. For two-wheelers and three-wheelers, the target is 80% of total sales by 2030, translating to an ambitious 80 million EVs on Indian roads.

demand_drivers.description: Two-wheelers remain a primary mode of personal transport across diverse geographies in India, driving consistent sales.

demand_drivers.driver: Rising middle-class income and young population
demand_drivers.description: Demographic and economic factors continue to fuel demand for accessible and affordable mobility solutions.

market_sizing.methodology: Total domestic sales of two-wheelers in India for FY26 (including both ICE and EV models).

demand_drivers.description: Three-wheelers are crucial for urban and semi-urban passenger transport and goods delivery, driving their sustained demand.
State-level policies and central schemes support the adoption of electric three-wheelers, particularly for commercial use.

market_sizing.methodology: Total domestic sales of three-wheelers in India for FY26 (including both ICE and EV models, passenger and goods carriers).

demand_drivers.description: Two-wheelers remain the most affordable and widely accessible personal transportation mode for a large segment of the Indian population.
Navigating congested urban and rural areas makes compact two-wheelers a practical choice for daily commute.

market_sizing.methodology: Market share of two-wheelers in the total domestic Indian auto market during April-December 2025 (FY26*). This indicates two-wheelers' dominant position in the overall vehicle sales landscape.

demand_drivers.description: Growth in the total number of two-wheelers and three-wheelers on the road drives demand for replacement parts and maintenance services.
As vehicles age, the frequency and need for repair and replacement parts increase, boosting aftermarket demand.

market_sizing.methodology: Projection for the domestic aftermarket auto-component market specifically for the two-wheelers and three-wheelers segment by 2030.

demand_drivers.description: Favorable policies and financial support schemes for electric vehicles accelerate consumer purchases.
Increasing understanding of cost savings and environmental benefits drives demand for E2Ws.

market_sizing.methodology: E2W sales in March 2025, demonstrating significant monthly growth for electric two-wheelers.

demand_drivers.description: E3Ws are increasingly favored for cost-effective and eco-friendly goods and passenger transport in urban areas.
State and central government initiatives promote the electrification of commercial fleets, including three-wheelers.

market_sizing.methodology: E3W sales in March 2026, indicating continued growth for electric three-wheelers.

demand_drivers.driver: State government incentives for EV manufacturing
demand_drivers.description: Tamil Nadu's policies, including capital subsidies, have attracted significant investment in EV production.
India's large and growing market for electric two-wheelers provides a stable base for manufacturing expansion.

market_sizing.methodology: Total current production capacity for EV two-wheelers in Tamil Nadu.

demand_drivers.description: Schemes like FAME II and EMPS 2024 offer direct incentives to purchasers of e-2Ws.

demand_drivers.driver: Increased income levels and favourable regulations
demand_drivers.description: Economic factors and state-specific policies, such as in Maharashtra, boost consumer adoption.

market_sizing.methodology: Total E-2W registrations in FY26, highlighting significant growth in the electric two-wheeler segment.

demand_drivers.description: Government targets for electrifying cargo and logistics fleets in states like Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh drive demand.
E-3Ws are essential for urban passenger transport and small-scale goods delivery, particularly in dense areas.

market_sizing.methodology: Total E-3W registrations in FY26, indicating continued growth in the electric three-wheeler segment.
